clue.text: Fancy spring water

parts.note: a spring is a natural source of water, a well
a well is also a source of water drawn from the ground

explanation.surface: An instruction to imagine some smart spring water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the water, but it is the exclamation of surprise, 'Fancy that!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of mild surprise, used interchangeably in speech.

clue.text: Run and see to make certain

definitions.meaning: to run along and see to something is to take steps so it happens
to guarantee that something will be the case

explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee an outcome is both to attend to it and to put it beyond doubt.

clue.text: Surveys faces perhaps

definitions.meaning: a verb: examines with the eyes, glances over
a plural noun: appearances, features as seen by others

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means gazes over; as a noun it means outward appearance, of which faces are an example.

clue.text: Ties up net anyhow and fishes

indicators.note: anyhow means in a haphazard way, so the letters of net are jumbled

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: Someone ties up a net carelessly before going fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyhow' makes ENT from NET.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl or catch something in knots is to bind it up, a synonym.

clue.text: Generous party?

definitions.meaning: the question mark flags the example

explanation.definitionFit: The word means openhanded, and it was also the name of a major British political party.

clue.text: One who demonstrates-when it's raining

explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'show' plus '-er' it is a demonstrator; read normally it is a short burst of rain.

clue.text: Sails around showing fibre

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of sails are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Sails moving around reveal the rope fibre they are made from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges SAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and twine.

clue.text: Recent offer made without hesitation outside the Bull

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the hesitation sound from the word offer

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

indicators.note: made here means put together anew, so the letters of recent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recent bid was put forward without a pause, near a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER from OFFER to leave OFF; 'made' rearranges RECENT into CENTRE. The Bull is the bullseye of a dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A dart landing beyond the bullseye has missed the middle, so it is not quite on target.

clue.text: Feelings allow movement in two directions

indicators.note: in says the word for movement sits inside the two compass letters

parts.note: E and S, east and south, two compass points
movement is motion

explanation.surface: Emotions are said to permit movement both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTION goes between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings such as joy or anger are synonyms for the sentiments we experience.

clue.text: Accompany to a different sector

indicators.note: different asks for the letters of sector in another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go along with another person to a new district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges SECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany someone is to go with them as a guard or companion, a synonym.

clue.text: Superlatively good infantry brigade should be put forward

parts.note: the superlative of good is best
foot soldiers are the infantry, called the Foot

explanation.surface: The finest foot soldiers deserve to be sent into the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the idiom 'put your best foot forward', meaning make your finest effort.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom, this is what one advances first to make a good impression.

clue.text: First robber ropes in another who goes to jail

indicators.note: another is read as an other, a different arrangement of the letters
First picks the opening letter of the word robber

explanation.surface: A leading thief brings in an accomplice who ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the first letter of 'robber', joins ROPES IN, and 'another' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in jail is an inmate or convict.

clue.text: Lucite could be a remedy for pestilence

definitions.note: the noun stands for the adjective meaning of pestilence or plague

indicators.note: a remedy fixes or alters, so the letters of Lucite could be put right as a new word

explanation.surface: A clear plastic might cure a plague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be a remedy' rearranges LUCITE, a trade name for acrylic plastic. The answer derives from Latin 'lues', plague; it now means syphilitic.
explanation.definitionFit: Lues is Latin for a plague or contagion, and this adjective describes such a disease.

clue.text: Spill the beans about imp, bound to be confined by itself

indicators.note: about means the word for confessing goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing, spilling the beans
an elf is a mischievous imp
a bound is a limit

explanation.surface: A confession about a sprite who must be restrained by its own nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spill the beans' looks like a confession to be defined, but it is slang wordplay; the definition is the last phrase, describing something that limits itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that restricts its own course, as a disease that ends without treatment, is restrained by its own nature.

clue.text: You'll find them around steamship

parts.note: the people around you on board a vessel are your fellow crew members

explanation.definitionFit: Fellow sailors serving on one vessel are crewmates, found all around on board.

clue.text: Top journalist following unruly crowd of 49 is moved

indicators.note: following says the journalist comes after the other pieces

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
IL is 49 in Roman numerals, fifty less one
ED is short for editor, the top journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: An editor follows a rowdy throng of forty-nine and is stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: IL for 49 is an irregular Roman numeral (the standard form is XLIX) that crosswords often use.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops or resources set in motion for action have been mustered, a sense close to moved.

clue.text: Ban on refreshment here? No, exactly the opposite

definitions.text: Ban on refreshment here? No, exactly the opposite

parts.words: Ban on refreshment here? No, exactly the opposite
parts.note: swap the idea round: not a bar on a snack but a place where snacks are served at a bar

explanation.definitionFit: A counter selling light meals is a café-style buffet, the reverse of forbidding food.

clue.text: There's no solution for this clue

definitions.text: There's no solution for this clue

parts.words: There's no solution for this clue
parts.note: read chemically, something with no solution cannot be dissolved in any liquid

explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be dissolved, or a bond that cannot be broken, is permanent.

clue.text: Alison and I formed an alliance

indicators.note: formed means shaped into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alison and the speaker teamed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' rearranges ALISON and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A close working connection or romantic relationship is a link, a synonym for an alliance.

clue.text: Medium sort of environment

definitions.meaning: the surroundings or setting in which something exists

explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word means one's surroundings, a medium in which one lives, and particularly a social background.

clue.text: Fish for the little devil I'm after

indicators.note: after says the single letter comes behind the word for a rascal

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous little devil
I'm read as I am, so the letter I is what comes after

explanation.surface: Someone wants seafood for the mischievous child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm after' reads as 'I am after': I follows SCAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails are served as a seafood dish.

clue.text: Dope removed a couple of points from dreadful edition

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the remaining letters are badly mangled
removed says two compass letters are taken out of the word edition

parts.note: E and N, east and north, two compass points

explanation.surface: A drug was taken out of an awful printing of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes E and N out of EDITION, leaving DITIO, and 'dreadful' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is slang for a fool or simpleton.

clue.text: Novice puts article in the loft and goes to sea

indicators.note: in places the novice and the article inside the word for a loft

parts.note: an attic is a loft
L is for learner, a novice
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A beginner stores an item in the attic and then heads off to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars; 'goes to' merely links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic is the ocean between Europe and the Americas, an example of a sea in the broad sense.

clue.text: Some bananas always affect the nose

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few bananas can always alter how the nose works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' marks the run NASAL hidden in 'bananas always'.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, the adjective describes whatever relates to the nose, as in a nasal spray.

clue.text: Sailor colours and refuses to drink

parts.note: AB is able-bodied seaman, a sailor
stains means colours, as a verb

explanation.surface: A sailor dyes things and turns down alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, an able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teetotal declines alcohol, which is the verb's commonest sense.

clue.text: Song bird is found in the hide!

indicators.note: found in tells us the little word is set inside the word for a hide

parts.note: a hide is an animal skin

explanation.surface: A songbird turns up in the birdwatchers' shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hide' seems to be the birdwatching hut, but it is an animal's SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch, a songbird.

clue.text: Steep right bend already arranged

indicators.note: to bend is to twist out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sharp right-hand curve on a road has been planned in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bend' rearranges STEEP and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Settings fixed beforehand, as on a dial, are determined in advance.

clue.text: Dreadful sound, almost loud inside, and with many bumps

indicators.note: inside says the shortened word sits within the jumbled letters
dreadful suggests the letters of sound are mangled
almost means the word loud loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A terrible noise, nearly deafening within, is full of lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges the letters of 'sound' into NODUS, and 'almost' drops the final letter of 'loud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in nodules, small knobs or lumps, is a synonym for being knobbly.
